memory_update.text: HWM is the public reference leader for the domestic-content aerospace components node, but its size and attention level make it a benchmark rather than the main underfollowed alpha target.

ATI should remain in the underfollowed lane despite large-cap size because its exposure is upstream in specialty alloys, titanium, forgings, and machined components rather than headline defense prime contracts.

RBC is a plausible underfollowed component/certification play due to AS9100/NADCAP evidence, aerospace bearing capacity, machined components, engine-part examples, and Boeing approvals, but customer concentration and defense program exposure require filing-level verification.

SIF is a below-$300M speculative exception with unusually direct node evidence: critical aerospace/defense components, titanium/aluminum/high-temperature alloys, AS9100D/ISO 9001, NADCAP certifications, and key OEM approvals.

The strongest falsification test for this node is whether companies can show actual domestic/compliant sourcing, customer approvals, incremental awards, backlog conversion, or capacity utilization benefits rather than merely having aerospace certifications.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C/2 pass to map customer edges from HWM, ATI, RBC, and SIF to GE Aerospace, RTX/Pratt & Whitney, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Safran, and military engine programs; current evidence supports capability, not yet share-gain causality.

node: Domestic-content aerospace and defense components: castings, forgings, precision machining, alloys, fasteners, and engine subcomponents
summary: Layer 1B expanded the direct public-company universe around domestic-content aerospace and defense components. The reference lane is anchored by Howmet as the most obvious public pure-play supplier of aero-engine, fastener, forging, casting, titanium, and structural products. The underfollowed lane highlights ATI and RBC Bearings as larger but less thematically crowded suppliers with direct aerospace materials/component exposure, and SIFCO as a micro-cap speculative exception with unusually direct evidence of titanium/aluminum/high-temperature-alloy aerospace component capability plus AS9100/NADCAP credentials. The node remains a hypothesis: policy, tariff, Buy American, and defense-supply-chain scrutiny could reroute share toward already-qualified domestic or compliant suppliers, but company-level domestic-content advantage still needs verification in filings, customer awards, and sourcing disclosures.
